result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.dfs_labeled_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Get every step of a depth-first search, each edge labeled by what the search did. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.dfs_labeled_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Get every step of a depth-first search, each edge labeled by what the search did. title: >- [Graph.dfs_labeled_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Get every step of a depth-first search, each edge labeled by what the search did. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get every step of a depth-first search, each edge labeled by what the search did. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L56072-L56184){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.dfs_labeled_edges( source=None, depth_limit=None, mode="out", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![DFS labeled edges](../assets/graphs/dfs-labeled-edges.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A triangle A, B, C with a tail C to D, searched depth-first from A (outlined). The tree edges A-B, B-C and C-D are numbered in the accent color; the dashed edge C-A leads to a node already visited. The card groups the thirteen labeled edges by kind: forward for A, A (the root) and the three tree edges, nontree for B-A, C-B, C-A, D-C and A-C, and reverse as the search backs up from D, C and B and finishes at A." width="100%"} `dfs_edges()` gives only the edges that discover new nodes. This gives the full transcript: every edge the search looks at, in order, and every time it backs up, each tagged with one of these labels: - `"forward"`: the search reaches `v` for the first time, from `u`. Each tree also starts with `(root, root, "forward")`. - `"nontree"`: `v` was already visited, so the edge is not followed. In an undirected graph this includes looking back at the node it came from. - `"reverse"`: the search is done with `v` and backs up to `u`. Each tree ends with `(root, root, "reverse")`. - `"reverse-depth_limit"`: `v` is `depth_limit=` hops from the root, so the search turns back without exploring it. The labels are what classic DFS algorithms are built from: discovery and finishing times (`"forward"` and `"reverse"`), back edges for cycle detection, and the low-point values behind articulation points and strongly connected components. They also make a step-by-step record for animating or teaching a search. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The starting node, as an integer ID or a string label. If `None` (default), search from every unvisited node in ID order, covering the whole graph. [depth_limit]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Do not explore nodes more than this many hops from the start of each tree. If `None` (default), there is no limit. [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which way to follow edges on a directed graph: `"out"` (default), `"in"`, or `"all"`. Ignored for undirected graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple[int, int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(u, v, label)` triples of node IDs and a label, in the order the search made them. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the node does not exist, `depth_limit=` is negative, or `mode=` is invalid. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~dfs_edges`) : Just the edges that discover new nodes. [](`~edge_dfs`) : Every edge in depth-first order, by edge ID. ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Neighbors are explored in edge insertion order, the same order `dfs_edges()` uses, so the `"forward"` edges between distinct nodes are exactly `dfs_edges()`. A neighbor joined by parallel edges is looked at once, and a self-loop gives one `"nontree"` step. Matches NetworkX's `dfs_labeled_edges`, except with `depth_limit=0`: NetworkX then still steps to the root's neighbors (as with `depth_limit=1`), while EdgeCase reports only the root, as `dfs_edges(depth_limit=0)` does. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A triangle with a tail. The search goes A, B, C, finds that C's neighbor A has been visited (`"nontree"`), goes on to D, and backs up when each node is done: ::: {#ee431e7f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(list("ABCD")) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D")]) label = g.get_label_from_id [(label(u), label(v), kind) for u, v, kind in g.dfs_labeled_edges("A")] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [('A', 'A', 'forward'), ('A', 'B', 'forward'), ('B', 'A', 'nontree'), ('B', 'C', 'forward'), ('C', 'B', 'nontree'), ('C', 'A', 'nontree'), ('C', 'D', 'forward'), ('D', 'C', 'nontree'), ('C', 'D', 'reverse'), ('B', 'C', 'reverse'), ('A', 'B', 'reverse'), ('A', 'C', 'nontree'), ('A', 'A', 'reverse')] ``` ::: ::: On an undirected graph, a `"nontree"` edge to any node other than the one the search came from closes a cycle, which gives a quick cycle test: ::: {#3a659e94 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} def has_cycle(graph): parent = {} for u, v, kind in graph.dfs_labeled_edges(): if kind == "forward": parent[v] = u elif kind == "nontree" and parent.get(u) != v: return True return False has_cycle(g), has_cycle(ec.Graph().add_path_graph(5)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: :::
